approved_findings: The new capture is a 765-line full iOS app-to-web Checkout guide, not a navigation index. The US iOS digital-goods scope and StoreKit storefront test remain (old:10-18; new:13-21); Android US direct in-app processing is a separate route, and Managed Payments is an optional merchant-of-record guide (old:8,12,555-557; new:9,15,751-753). A captured statement does not establish current regional eligibility or App Store approval.

New raw:26,30-36 adds a customer-configured Accounts v2 path, explicitly generally available for Connect users but public preview for other Stripe users, with preview-version and Dashboard preview instructions for preview participants. It recommends Accounts for most use cases; Customers v1 remains a full branch at new:227-256,419-524. Old raw:22-25,143-172,228-332 only modeled Customer v1. Current source:13,27-28,54-65,82-88 implies Customer-only; update those sections with separate qualified v2/v1 identities and examples, not a universal replacement.

Accounts v2 examples create stripe.v2.core.accounts at new:198-219 and pass customer_account in one-time and subscription Checkout Sessions at new:345-358,391-404. The older Customers v1 examples still pass customer at new:451-464,498-511. New integration_identifier appears in both paths as an integration label/conversion-measurement example (new:356-357,402-403,462-463,509-510); it is not evidence of a required field or realized conversion tracking.

New raw:11 adds Checkout studio configure/preview navigation, and new:755-757 adds optional yearly-subscription monthly-term and tax display settings. Neither changes the US iOS eligibility premise. The old/new Universal Links, Safari, StoreKit gate, and checkout.session.completed fulfillment instructions persist (old:174-226,334-378,427-431; new:258-310,526-570,620-624).

Current source:27-32 lists Checkout redirect at step 5 before server receipt and entitlement grant at step 6, while both captures explain Checkout waits for webhook acknowledgement before redirect or falls back after 10 seconds if not acknowledged (old:429-431; new:620-624). Replace the strict sequence with a separately timed return and server-owned fulfillment. More importantly, checkout.session.completed and success_url do not alone prove paid funds when optional dynamic methods are enabled (new:417,524). Related pinned authority wiki/sources/source-stripe-checkout-dashboard-payment-methods.md:22-34 states delayed methods can leave completed with payment_status unpaid; grant coins only for paid status, or on checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded, and handle async_payment_failed. Concept wiki/concepts/stripe-checkout.md:140,202-204 agrees; its :212 shorthand must be read with the paid-status qualification.

Current source Swift excerpt at source:69-80 sets paymentComplete from a success URL substring and omits the raw guide's instruction to fetch latest customer entitlements from the server (old:365-371; new:557-563). Treat this as illustrative UI handling only; paid status plus trusted server entitlement state control credits. The shared raw webhook sample has an inherited JavaScript block-scope error: old:447-474 and new:641-668 declare let event inside if (webhookSecret) and later read event.data.object outside it, so either branch fails before identity lookup. It also uses session.customer at new:666-673 while the new Accounts v2 Session supplies customer_account at new:354,400. Do not present either v1 or v2 sample as an executable fulfillment implementation.

Require payment_status paid before grant, use async_payment_succeeded for later clearance, and handle async_payment_failed; a success_url or completed event alone is not paid finality. Neither v1 nor v2 sample is verified runnable fulfillment code; the v2 identity mapping remains unresolved.
